newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: New competitor to enter Bogota telephone market.
newsitem.headline: New competitor to enter Bogota telephone market.

text.p: BOGOTA, April 15 Reuter - State-run Empresas Publicas de Medellin said it had entered into a strategic partnership with Japan's Itochu Corporation to begin providing telephone service in the Colombia capital by year-end.
The consortium would be the second to enter the Bogota market in a bid to break up the monopoly long enjoyed by city-owned Empresa de Telecomunicaciones de Bogota ETB.

Empresas Publicas de Medellin currently provides all public services in the northwest city of Medellin and outlying townships. Its manager, Fernando Panesso, told Reuters its joint venture with Itochu called for the installation of 100,000 new phone lines in the capital at a cost of $100 million.

The first of the fiber optic phone lines will begin operating before year's end, he said, adding that more lines could be installed in the near future. "We think demand is a lot higher than the 100,000 but we have to go step-by-step," Panesso said. Bogota, a city of 6 million, currently boasts no more than about 1.5 million phone lines.

Capitel, a firm formed by Ericsson, NEC, Nortel Northern Telecom, Siemens and state-run Empresa Nacional de Telecomunicaciones Telecom, announced plans in February to install 550,000 phone lines in Bogota in 1997/98 at cost of $513 million. (-- Javier Mozzo, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944)
